title: Chapter 39
content:
Jakyeong sat on the open café terrace, watching the morning foot traffic drift past. Since landing in Korea, he had been thrown from one chaotic operation into another without a moment to catch his breath; sitting here in the sun, leisurely sipping an iced coffee, felt like a stolen slice of ordinary freedom. Inside the glass-walled café, clusters of students around his age—or slightly younger—were huddled over textbooks and laptops, lost in their studies.

Jakyeong leaned his head back against the wrought-iron chair. The broken sleep from the night before left a dull ache behind his eyes.

A car door clicked shut by the curb.

Straightening up, he saw Kang Il-hyun stepping away from a parked sedan and striding across the sidewalk toward the terrace.

Il-hyun pulled out the opposing chair, dropping his heavy key fob onto the metal table. "You look like you didn't catch a wink of sleep. Your face is completely drawn."

Without waiting for permission, Il-hyun reached across the table, picked up Jakyeong’s coffee, and took a long, unapologetic draught. "Excuse me. My throat was parched."

Jakyeong offered no reaction, watching him with flat, unblinking eyes.

Crossing one long leg over the other, Il-hyun leaned back in his seat, his index finger tapping a slow, rhythmic beat against the tabletop. The steady, measured cadence carried the suffocating weight of a ticking clock.

When the couple at the adjacent table finally gathered their bags and left, leaving the terrace deserted, Jakyeong finally broke the silence.

"I accept your terms."

The tapping finger froze. A slow, knowing smile spread across Il-hyun’s lips.

Beneath the table, Jakyeong clenched his fists tight. "On one condition."

"Name it."

"Triple the fee."

Il-hyun’s expression went completely neutral. Triple meant fifteen million dollars—roughly eighteen billion won. An astronomical figure for a single contract.

"If I'm breaking contract with Chairman Kang, I need enough to cover the breach penalties once the dust settles," Jakyeong said evenly.

"A penalty clause? Because you failed to put a bullet through my heart?"

"Yes."

"Even for that, isn't fifteen million a bit steep?"

Jakyeong met his dark gaze without flinching. "Compared to what you stand to gain from this... isn't that pocket change?"

"Look at you, talking big," Il-hyun chuckled, tilting his head. "Dismissing eighteen billion won as pocket change."

"If you can't meet the price, I walk away from both sides."

Jakyeong made to stand, but Il-hyun slid off his sunglasses, tilting his chin upward. Sizing up the client was standard tradecraft, but for an operative working for hire, this kid was remarkably unyielding.

Il-hyun made a small downward gesture with his fingers. Taking the hint, Jakyeong sat back down, reaching for the glass of iced water beside him instead of the coffee.

An amused scoff rumbled in Il-hyun's chest. The fake Jang Yi-an sitting across from him was brazen beyond belief. He hadn't expected the boy to cower, but demanding an extortionate bonus on the spot was a delightful surprise.

After a beat of calculation, Il-hyun gave a slow, deliberate nod.

"Fine. Fifteen million dollars. Half up front, and the remaining balance upon completion."

"The advance must clear my account before the trigger date."

"Wiring that sum through clean offshore channels takes time. Give me three to four days."

Jakyeong gave a curt nod. "Are we settled, then?"

"We are."

"Good."

"Then I believe you owe me an answer."

Jakyeong frowned. What answer was left to give? The man already knew the mastermind and the broker. "I have no idea what you're referring to."

"Your real name," Il-hyun drawled, leaning in. "Because it certainly isn't Jang Yi-an."

Jakyeong kept his lips sealed. He had worn over a dozen aliases in his lifetime. When the Wang family first took him off the streets, they registered him as Wang Wei, and countless operational handles had followed since.

Yet deep down, he had always held onto his original name. As much as he despised the blood running in his veins, the name itself was the only piece of his identity that belonged entirely to him.

Seeing the stubborn silence, Il-hyun let out a dry, exasperated laugh. "Come now. After agreeing to eighteen billion won, surely you can spare two syllables?"

Jakyeong hesitated, his jaw tightening before his lips parted.

"Lee..."

"Lee?"

"Lee..."

Il-hyun’s eyes narrowed into sharp, expectant slits, silently demanding the rest.

Cornered, Jakyeong finally muttered the words: "...Lee Ja-kyeong."

"Lee. Ja. Kyeong."

Il-hyun pronounced each syllable slowly, rolling the sounds across his tongue as if savoring a fine vintage. Hearing his true name spoken aloud in that deep baritone felt profoundly strange. Even within his inner circle, barely anyone outside Dmitri and Wang Han knew his birth name.

Regret flared instantly, but taking it back now was impossible.

"Your age?"

"Is that relevant to the contract?"

"I'm curious. Tell me."

"Twenty-five."

"Ah, four years younger than me. And your parents?"

Jakyeong’s brow furrowed in irritation. Giving up his name was one thing, but enduring a full family background check was ridiculous.

When he refused to answer, Il-hyun rested his chin on his palm, tilting his head with an unhurried, predatory gaze. A stray summer breeze rustled the floral centerpiece between them.

"I simply want to know."

"Dead," Jakyeong said flatly. "None."

"A lover?"

Jakyeong glared back in cold silence.

Reading the glare, Il-hyun’s lips curved into a bright, satisfied smirk.

"Perfect. No lovers, no parents."

"..."

With a light chuckle, Il-hyun pushed his chair back and rose to his feet. "Let's head back to the estate. For the time being, you're still Jang Yi-an."

[Dmitri, that son of a bitch.]

Wang Han’s furious growl crackled through the encrypted receiver. With Dmitri flipping his loyalty to Kang Il-hyun, their entire operational structure had been compromised.

Double-brokering wasn't unheard of in the underworld—where money reigned supreme, nobody faulted a contractor for following the highest bidder. But Jakyeong had always prioritized professional integrity alongside his fee. Accepting Il-hyun's counter-offer felt like stepping into a trap that could snap shut on his ankles at any moment.

[Are you truly going through with this?]

"Yes."

[Do you actually trust that bastard?]

Jakyeong hesitated. Could he trust Kang Il-hyun? He had turned the question over in his mind a hundred times without reaching a clean answer. But with Il-hyun holding all the leverage, walking away wasn't an option on the table.

"There's no other play."

[Should I fly into Seoul?]

"No. If you move, it will draw too much heat. Stay in Hong Kong and keep tabs on Dmitri's channels—there's a chance the two of them are coordinating behind our backs."

[Can you handle this alone?]

"Don't worry. Ryun is here. I'll collect the final payout and return in one piece."

A heavy, resigned sigh bled through the line. If Wang Han knew Jakyeong had already breached an offshore syndicate vessel and executed a target last night, he would have lost his mind completely.

After confirming the account details for the offshore wire transfer, Jakyeong ended the call, letting out a long breath of his own.

Ever since returning from the café, a dull migraine had been throbbing against his temples. Searching the suite turned up no painkillers, so he buzzed the house intercom to request a dose. Heading downstairs and risking an awkward encounter with Il-hyun was something he preferred to avoid.

Resting his head back against the headboard, a soft knock sounded at the bedroom door.

Assuming the maid had arrived, Jakyeong swung his legs off the bed—only for the door to open, revealing Kang Il-hyun.

Jakyeong’s face pulled into an immediate, undisguised scowl.

Il-hyun stepped inside without hesitation, carrying a silver tray with a glass of water and two white tablets. "I heard you had a headache. Are you feeling alright?"

Jakyeong gave a curt, dismissive nod. "I'm fine... Just need some rest."

Il-hyun set the tray on the side table. When Jakyeong moved to take the opposite armchair, Il-hyun caught his wrist, hauling him firmly onto the sofa cushion right beside him.

Given their new contractual dynamic, drawing a blade was out of the question, forcing Jakyeong to endure the proximity.

Il-hyun picked up the tablets and held them out. As Jakyeong reached to take them, Il-hyun pulled his hand back, parting his own lips in an exaggerated Ah.

Not this again.

Jakyeong glared with pure contempt, only for Il-hyun to let out a low, oily chuckle. "Look at that. You don't even bother faking a polite smile anymore, do you? Now that the mask is off?"

Seizing the split second Il-hyun glanced away, Jakyeong snatched the pills from his fingers, tossed them back, and washed them down with a gulp of water.

As the tablets slid down his throat, a sharp, bitter chemical burn flared in his esophagus, radiating a strange heat through his chest. Did I swallow it wrong?

Brushing a hand against his throat, he caught the sly, wicked grin spreading across Il-hyun's face.

An icy dread gripped Jakyeong’s spine.

He shoved two fingers down his throat to force a gag, but Il-hyun caught his wrist in an iron grip. Jakyeong wrenched his arm free and surged upward, but Il-hyun tackled him around the waist, using his superior mass to slam Jakyeong flat across the sofa cushions.

Hovering directly above him, Il-hyun’s eyes were dark, heavy, and dangerous.

Within seconds, Jakyeong felt his breathing grow shallow. A thick, paralyzing languor washed through his limbs, turning his muscles to lead.

"The more I think about it, the more wronged I feel," Il-hyun murmured against his ear.

"Get off me..."

"Even a cheap roadside diner throws in complimentary side dishes. Yet I just handed you eighteen billion won, and I haven't received a single ounce of service."

Jakyeong grimaced, knowing precisely what kind of "service" the bastard had in mind.

Il-hyun reached down, slowly peeling away the medical bandage covering Jakyeong’s throat. The angry crimson bruise beneath was fully exposed—an eyesore that had been grating on Il-hyun's nerves since yesterday. Uncovering the conspiracy in Hong Kong hadn't made him half as furious as seeing that mark.

Jakyeong felt his core heating up, an unnatural, desperate throb pulsing in his lower belly. He tried shoving Il-hyun's shoulders away, but his drugged limbs possessed zero leverage.

Tracing a thumb over the bruised skin on Jakyeong's neck, Il-hyun whispered in a venomous rasp:

"Going out and getting yourself branded like cattle the moment my back is turned... Fuck. It's truly infuriating."

Il-hyun leaned down to claim his mouth, but Jakyeong brought a heavy palm up, clamping it flat over Il-hyun's lips.

"If you're looking for a warm body for the night... find someone else. I have zero interest in men."

With his mouth covered, Il-hyun didn't pull back. Instead, his hand slid straight down, slipping past Jakyeong’s waistband into his briefs.

Beneath the cotton, Jakyeong’s shaft was already rock-hard, slick with pre-cum from the aphrodisiac burning through his veins. Jakyeong grabbed Il-hyun’s forearm in a desperate attempt to break the hold, but the man ignored the resistance completely—wrapping a large, warm palm around the rigid length and pumping in steady, deliberate strokes.

A fuse sparked in Jakyeong’s mind as a wave of involuntary pleasure breached his defenses. He bit down on his lower lip to stifle a groan.

Leaning close to his ear, Il-hyun whispered, "Claiming you have no interest... while your cock is weeping in my hand?"

Rage and humiliation snapped the last thread of Jakyeong’s restraint. "You motherfucker! That's because you drugged me—!"

Il-hyun’s mouth crashed down, swallowing the curse whole.

Jakyeong snapped his teeth shut, driving his incisors hard into Il-hyun’s bottom lip. Despite the searing pain, Il-hyun didn't flinch—forcing his tongue past the bloody barrier to tangle fiercely with Jakyeong’s.

Trying to shove the invading tongue away only resulted in a wet, sliding friction that stoked the fire between their hips, making the rhythm of Il-hyun's hand down below even more ruthless.

When Il-hyun finally broke the seal for a fraction of a second, Jakyeong lunged, sinking his teeth into the flesh of Il-hyun's lower lip with savage force, tearing the skin.

A low grunt tore from Il-hyun's throat as he pulled back.

Heavy droplets of dark crimson blood dripped from his torn lip, landing on Jakyeong’s pale cheek and collarbone.

Wiping the back of his hand across his bleeding mouth, Kang Il-hyun let out a chilling, thoroughly unhinged grin.

"So that's how we're playing it?"
